0.long_answer: Levodopa is the medication commonly prescribed for dopamine-responsive dystonia and is also used to treat autosomal recessive GTP cyclohydrolase I deficiency. This drug works by increasing dopamine levels in the brain, which helps to alleviate the symptoms of dystonia and other motor disturbances associated with these conditions. In many cases, levodopa is administered in combination with a dopa decarboxylase inhibitor, such as carbidopa, to enhance its efficacy and reduce peripheral side effects.
